chat.author: Eisha Raazia
chat.text: This question is generally for all the participants as well as organizers, what advice would you give to an undergrad joining an IETF meeting for the first time. Since the lack of knowledge and presence of experienced people in the room can be intimidating.

chat.author: Steve Traugott
chat.text: @Eisha Raazia I'm new here too, but as someone who has participated in and helped lead tech conferences for decades, I can assure you that much of the energy and innovation in any community comes from the youngest people in it.  I've seen entire industry segments being launched by people who are undergrad or recent grads who got an idea or spark of inspiration during their first conference and ran with it.

chat.author: Steve Traugott
chat.text: For anyone else trying to figure out how to get to the meetecho top bar that Jay showed in session 1 -- I finally realized that your zoom setting might be hiding it.  For me (Chrome on Linux) I had to set the zoom to 150% to see the top bar with icons for collaborative note app, show of hands, transcription, etc.  Any less wouldn't show it.

chat.author: Michelle Cotton
chat.text: @Eisha it is challenging to network remotely.  In the chat for WG meetings, if you find someone talking about something you are interested in, you can direct message them in Meetecho.
